**Starts** once #48 is merged.

## Why

The coordinator can't plan stays and stops until it can read the trip it's building, and look up places. `read_itinerary` gives it the whole trip, or one part of it, as short lines (technical spec 7.2). `find_place` and `read_place` let it turn a name, such as "Moab", into a place, and answer questions about that place.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 2.1 (`read_itinerary`), 2.3 (`find_place` and `read_place`), and 4.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 7.2.

## Open questions

- ~~What's the size limit on an in-process MCP tool's result? Claude Code may cut off large results. The limit for MCP tools is believed to be 25,000 tokens, but it hasn't been checked for in-process servers.~~ Settled 2026-10-23 in chat: the limit is 25,000 tokens. That's the default in the Claude Code that SDK 0.3.301 ships (2.1.301), and nothing found in it treats in-process servers differently. A result over it is saved to a file, and the model gets the file's path and a short preview. The coordinator has no Read tool, so for it the result is cut off. So `read_itinerary` checks its own reply, and returns an error instead of a reply over 25,000 tokens. A full read is fine while trips stay under the limit. If one goes over, the fix is to rethink the four uses of a full read (technical spec 5.2), not to raise the limit.
- ~~How does `read_itinerary` get its check results? A read runs `FeasibilityChecker.workOut()` and `compare()`, and saves nothing (domain model 4.8). But `TripReader.read()` hands back only the trip. PR #35 creates the checker only inside `TripWriter`'s finish, from the settings, the clock, and the write's calendar. The read tool needs the same: a calendar and a checker for the trip it read. Raised in PR #35.~~ Settled 2026-10-23 in chat: the tool makes them, the way `look_up_stay_weather` does in `src/tools/weather-tools.ts`. It reads the trip with `TripReader.read()`, and gets the calendar from `calendarAndServicesFor(trip, settings, now)`. Then it creates a `FeasibilityChecker` from the trip brief, the settings, and that calendar, runs `workOut()` on the itinerary, and runs `compare()` against the itinerary's saved check results. The comparison marks each result new or already known. Nothing is saved. `TripSession` (`src/tools/trip-session.ts`) gets the full `settings` in place of `limits`, plus `now`, as `WeatherSession` has. `TripReader` stays as it is. This keeps the layers one way: tools use persistence and the domain, persistence uses the domain, and the domain uses neither.
- ~~Put the itinerary into the line the app adds after a resume. Technical spec 5.2 gives the line as "This session was resumed. Read the trip brief, the itinerary, and memory first." Until `read_itinerary` exists, the coordinator can't read the itinerary, so #48 left it out. Its line, `RESUMED_LINE` in `src/agent/app-lines.ts`, says "Read the trip brief and memory first." The coordinator's instructions say the same in their section on reading the trip brief and memory. Both get the itinerary added here. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-23, while #48 was being built.~~ Settled 2026-10-23 in chat:
  - `RESUMED_LINE` becomes technical spec 5.2's line word for word: "This session was resumed. Read the trip brief, the itinerary, and memory first." The comment above it about #54 comes out.
  - The instructions section "Reading the trip brief and memory" in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` becomes "Reading the trip brief, the itinerary, and memory". Its first bullet becomes "At the start of a session, before your first reply, read the trip brief, the whole itinerary, and memory." Its second becomes "After a resume, read all three again before changing anything. Another session may have changed the trip, and a session of another trip may have changed user memory." Its third, on reading memory again, stays.
  - The section gets one more bullet, on warnings still open from an earlier session (technical spec 5.2), such as: "In your first reply, briefly mention warnings that are still open, such as 'Still open from last time: the trip is 4 days, and you asked for 5.'"
  - The offer to rerun the weather worker when a forecast is now available waits for #64, which builds that worker.

## Do

- Add `find_place` and `read_place` on the `places` server, and give them to the coordinator. `read_place` checks the place belongs to the session's trip.
- Add `read_itinerary`, for the whole trip or scoped to a day, stay, or stop. Leave out route lines.
- Add the itinerary to the resume line and to the coordinator's instructions on reading at the start of a session, and the bullet on open warnings, as open question 3 says.
- Measure a full read of a 14-day trip: its characters, and its tokens as the API counts them.
- Make `read_itinerary` return an error when its reply would be over 25,000 tokens, such as "Can't read the itinerary: it's too large to return." The tool can't count tokens without calling the API, so it checks the reply's characters. Set that limit from the measured characters per token, with room to spare, so the tool stops before Claude Code's limit would.

## Done when

- In a chat with the coordinator, it resolves "Moab," and answers "is Milt's open on Mondays?" from `read_place`. Milt's is a stop on Moab Day 2, in the example trip in domain model section 5.2.
- Tests on the example trips (domain model, section 5) show what each scope returns.
- The measured size, the 25,000-token limit, and the error are written into tool design section 2.1. If the 14-day trip's full read is near the limit, Joe hears about it before #55 starts.
- A test shows a read over the limit returns the error.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-21-read-the-itinerary).
